messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Stan 1.0.1 Friday?
parts:
Now that we have the truncation model under control
(at least in the sense of not being buggy) and have
made a few patches elsewhere for error checking, I'd like
to roll out 1.0.1.

Daniel's plugged through the manual doing what I'm
ashamed to admit I didn't do the first time -- make
sure all the models in the doc compile.

We're also going to check all the functions in the manual
to make sure they're all declared in the function signatures
in stan/gm so that they're available.

Since we hadn't exposed normal_p, we'll change that
and the other cumulative distributions to normal_cdf
for 1.0.1. I don't imagine they'll get a lot of direct
use in models, but we'd need them for the censored
data model where the number of censoring points is known
but we don't want to impute missing values.

I'll get the Stan 1.0.1 release ready to go by tomorrow
afternoon at the latest. Hopefully Jiqiang can plug it
into RStan 1.0.1 tomorrow or Friday and we can release
1.0.1 on Friday.

I'm happy there are so few bugs being reported. (I'm
less happy at the trouble people are having with the
variable declarations and order dependency.)

- Bob
